We have
\[
5x_{i+1}-x_i-3x_ix_{i+1}=1.
\]
Rearrange as
\[
(5-3x_i)x_{i+1}=x_i+1.
\]
If \(x_i=\frac53\), this gives \(0=\frac83\), impossible. Hence
\[
x_{i+1}=\frac{x_i+1}{5-3x_i}.
\]

Define
\[
f(x)=\frac{x-1}{x-\frac13}.
\]
For \(x\neq \frac13\),
\[
f(x_{i+1})
=\frac{x_{i+1}-1}{x_{i+1}-\frac13}
=2\frac{x_i-1}{x_i-\frac13}
=2f(x_i).
\]

Now consider cases.

- If some \(x_i=\frac13\), the equation forces \(x_{i+1}=\frac13\). Going around the cycle, all \(x_i=\frac13\). Then
  \[
  x_1+\cdots+x_{42}=42\cdot \frac13=14.
  \]

- If no \(x_i=\frac13\), then applying the relation \(42\) times gives
  \[
  f(x_{43})=2^{42}f(x_1).
  \]
  Since \(x_{43}=x_1\),
  \[
  f(x_1)=2^{42}f(x_1),
  \]
  so \(f(x_1)=0\). Thus \(x_1=1\), and then all \(x_i=1\). The sum is
  \[
  42.
  \]

So the possible sums are \(42\) and \(14\). Their product is
\[
42\cdot 14=588.
\]

\[
\boxed{588}
\]
